newsitem.title: UK: Gencor puts shine on London as mining finance hub.
newsitem.headline: Gencor puts shine on London as mining finance hub.

text.p: For any major international mining company London is still the place to be for tapping capital markets.
Canada has gained much ground in recent years, but primarily remains a market for local companies, while Britain's capital continues to be the centre for the world's big players, analysts said.
"Certainly for international companies London is the major centre," said industry analyst Charles Kernot at Paribas Capital Markets.
His view was underlined by reports South Africa's Gencor Ltd is considering to list part of its operations here in a drive to boost its international operations.
UK newspapers said Gencor plans to retain a majority holding in the London-listed mining group which will have Billiton at its centre.
Billiton was bought by Gencor from Royal Dutch/Shell Group in 1994 for $1.2 billion.
Gencor itself was less specific, merely saying it might tap international markets to fund projects abroad.
South African currency restrictions forced Gencor to go to London to finance its expansion plans, analysts said.
Also, it would have been hard to find the money needed in Johannesburg, which is still too illiquid a market to attract substantial interest from foreign investors, they said.
Gencor would not be the first South African firm to turn to London and is unlikely to be the last.
Analysts reckon Avmin Ltd might also be tempted to turn to Britain to develop its exploration activities in Zambia.
Meanwhile, Randgold & Exploration Co Ltd is already in the process of organising "roadshows" to drum up investor interest for its imminent London listing.
In addition, JCI Ltd is negotiating a merger with Britain's Lonrho Plc which might result in a new entity with listings in both Johannesburg and London.
Mining companies from other emerging markets are also attracted to Britain's capital.

Indonesian state-controlled gold and nickel mining firm PT Aneka Tambang said in March it may seek a London listing, while Poland has plans to float up to 15 percent of the country's copper group KGHM Polska Miedz SA here.
The Observer newspaper here reported over the weekend that the businesses Gencor plans to float in London would be worth about one billion pounds ($1.6 billion).
That would put the new mining group in the same league as Lonrho which has a market capitalisation of 1.07 billion pounds. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
